• **Hydrological cycle** is a natural process where water is constantly moving between these three spheres.
 
• It involves various stages like **evaporation, condensation, precipitation, infiltration, **and **surface runoff.**
 
• This cycle is essential for maintaining life on Earth by providing water to all living organisms.
 
• The** hydrological cycle **helps regulate the climate, weather patterns, and erosion processes.

• **Hydrostatical equilibrium** is a condition in which the upward buoyant force equals the downward gravitational force on a fluid.
 
• **Water circulation** is a broader term that can encompass the movement of water in various systems, but it is not specifically used to describe the continuous process between the lithosphere, atmosphere, and hydrosphere.

questions.question: Article 50 of the Constitution of India refers to the ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**separation of judiciary from executive.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Article 50 **requires the state to separate the judiciary from the executive branch of government in public services. 
 
• The** article states that** the state should take steps to: 
 
 
• Prevent the unfair use of power or positions by authorities 
 
• Promote a democratic form of government 
 
• Ensure that each organ of government works independently 
 
• Maintain balance among all organs of government
 
 
 
• Article 50 is part of the** Directive Principles of State Policy**, which are **not enforceable.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are a set of guidelines in the Indian Constitution that guide the government in making laws and policies.
 
• The DPSPs are found in **Articles 36 to 51** of** Part IV** of the Constitution.
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) have been **amended four times** through the following amendments to the Indian Constitution:
 
• **42nd Amendment Act of 1976:** Added four new DPSPs, including **Articles 39, 39A, 43A, and 48A.** These DPSPs include: 
 
 
• Article 39: Securing opportunities for children's healthy development 
 
• Article 39A: Promoting equal justice and providing free legal aid to the poor 
 
• Article 43A: Securing workers' participation in industry management 
 
• Article 48A: Protecting and improving the environment, and safeguarding forests and wildlife 
 
 
 
• **44th Amendment Act of 1978: **Added a new DPSP under Article 38, which requires the state to reduce inequalities in income, status, facilities, and opportunities 
 
• **86th Amendment Act of 2002: **Changed the subject matter of Article 45 and made basic education a fundamental right under Article 21A 
 
• **97th Amendment Act of 2011: **Added a new DPSP for cooperative societies under Article 43B.

questions.question: If tax rate decreases with increase in taxable base, then this type of taxation is called:

__
 
• A regressive tax system is one in which the **tax rate decreases as the taxable amount (or income) increases.**
 
• In a regressive system, lower-income individuals pay a higher percentage of their income in taxes than higher-income individuals. 
 
• Regressive taxes can lead to** increased income inequality.**
 
• Examples of Regressive Taxes: **Sales Taxes, Excise Taxes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• This tax system imposes a** higher tax rate on higher-income earners.**
 
• As income increases, so does the tax rate, ensuring that wealthier individuals pay a larger proportion of their income in taxes.
 
 
 
• **Degressive taxation**
 
 
• It is a hybrid tax system** combining regressive and proportional taxation elements.**
 
• In a degressive tax system, the tax rate decreases as the income or taxable base increases, but not as drastically as in a regressive tax system.
 
• It starts with a progressive rate for lower income levels but eventually flattens out, so the tax burden becomes less steep for higher income brackets.
 
 
 
• **Increasing tax rate** system is the** same as progressive taxation.**

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT one of the factors leading to the economic reforms in 1991?

options.text: There was inflation in the economy.

questions.solution:

__
 
• The 1991 economic reforms in India were a response to **several factors**, including:

 
 
• **Balance of payments crisis**:- India's foreign currency reserves fell to a low in 1990-91, making it difficult to pay for imports.
 
• **Inflation**:- The inflation rate increased from** 6.7% to 16.7%** as the money supply grew rapidly.
 
• Fiscal deficit:- The government's** fiscal deficit increased** due to increased non-development expenditures.
 
• **Iraq War**:- The Iraq war contributed to **higher oil prices **and the Gulf nations stopped sending foreign money to India.
 
• **Poor performance of public sector enterprises**:- The performance of public sector enterprises was poor due to political involvement. 
 
 
 
• In 1991, as India faced a severe economic crisis, that time:-
 
 
• Prime MInister: **P. V. Narasimha Rao**
 
• Finance Minister: Manmohan Singh
 
• RBI Governor: **S. Venkitaramanan**

• **Inflation**: A broad increase in the price of goods and services across an economy. A low and steady rate of inflation is considered a sign of a healthy economy. 
 
• **Deflation**: A period when prices fall, which can negatively impact an economy. Deflation can lead to a decrease in investments and production, which can increase unemployment. 
 
• **Stagflation**: A rare phenomenon that occurs when there is high inflation combined with weak economic growth and high unemployment. Stagflation can be difficult to recover from because policies that curb inflation can also curb growth. 
 
• **Disinflation**: A period when the inflation rate falls, but remains positive. 
 
• **Phillips curve**: A theory that describes the relationship between inflation and recession, which were considered mutually exclusive in the version of Keynesian macroeconomic theory that was dominant between the end of World War II and the late 1970s. 
 
• **Monetary policy**: Central banks use monetary policy tools like the bank rate, repo rate, and statutory liquidity rate to increase or decrease the money supply in an economy.

questions.question: A hostel had food provision for 300 students for a month. After 20 days, 50 students left the hostel. How long would the remaining food last? (1 month = 30 days)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Remaining food for **300 students** is for **10 days** (30 − 20 = 10).

Students remaining = 300 − 50 = **250 students**.

Using **M₁D₁ = M₂D₂**: 300 × 10 = 250 × D.

D = 3000 ÷ 250 = **12 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca73f89cd369ca6a4a33ff132643a7593c8d0cac572a9e1735308b7c0c066bc5.png]

Total students = **300**

Total provision = **30 days**

Days elapsed = **20 days**

Students left = **50**

⇒ Total Work (Total food units) = 300 × 30 = **9000 units**

⇒ Food consumed in 20 days = 300 × 20 = **6000 units**

⇒ Remaining food = 9000 − 6000 = **3000 units**

⇒ Remaining students = 300 − 50 = **250 students**

⇒ Number of days food will last = 3000 ÷ 250

⇒ Days = **12 days**

**∴ The correct answer is 12 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Chain Rule (Work and Person)

The formula used is **M₁D₁H₁/W₁ = M₂D₂H₂/W₂**, where M is men, D is days, H is hours, and W is work.

Inverse Proportion

The number of **days** is **inversely proportional** to the number of **men** for a constant amount of food/work.
